# Measurement pitfalls

Every defect below was hit during the analysis that motivated this skill, and each one independently inverted a conclusion. The tools in this skill make them structurally impossible rather than warning about them — read this before trusting a number that came out of a modified pipeline.

**Self-reference.** The entity a hook names often includes the file the tool call was already acting on. That file is in the session's activity list because it was just touched, so crediting it scores nearly every emission as useful. In the analysis that motivated this skill this alone produced a reported 87.4% hit rate against a true figure near half (88% of blocks in that corpus named the touched file among their own anchors). Prevented by: [`outcomes.mjs`](../scripts/outcomes.mjs) excludes the entity equal to the originating tool call's own repo-relative path on every row — there is no flag or code path that skips this.

**Ordering.** Building the activity map across the whole session and asking "was this file ever touched" counts activity that happened *before* the emission. Prevented by: `outcomes.mjs` only counts activity-index entries with `ordinal > emission.ordinal` for `touched`/`written`, and `ordinal < emission.ordinal` for `seenBefore` — the two are structurally distinct fields, never merged.

**Censoring.** Emissions late in a session have little opportunity to be acted on. In the original analysis, anchors with 50-200 records remaining were acted on at 3%; those with 200+ at 24% — the single largest effect found, dominating any unadjusted "wasted" figure. Prevented by: `outcomes.mjs` reports `recordsLeft` on every row and never uses it to score a low-opportunity row as a failure; [`baseline.mjs`](../scripts/baseline.mjs) reports the enrichment ratio both overall and restricted to `--min-records-left` (default 200) so a reader can see the ratio survives the adjustment instead of taking the unadjusted figure on faith.

**Parse residue.** Rendered anchors carry human status suffixes (`path#L1-L2 — changed`). Splitting on `#` alone leaves ` — changed` attached to bare-path anchors, which then never match anything and score a false 0%. Prevented by: every extractor strips the ` — status` suffix before the `#Lstart-Lend` fragment, never the other order — see [`extractors/git-span.mjs`](../scripts/extractors/git-span.mjs)'s `stripAnchorSuffix`.

**Proxy metrics computed over a subset.** A median anchor width computed over line-ranged anchors only — silently skipping whole-file anchors — made a non-existent signal look decisive. This skill avoids the trap by not computing that metric at all: `baseline.mjs`'s crosstabs are restricted to fields every outcome row always carries (`seenBefore`, `recordsLeft`), not hook-specific proxies that could be computed over a biased subset.

**Interpreting a raw hit rate.** Without a baseline the number means nothing. In the original analysis, surfaced entities were touched at 17.2% against 13.3% for random files from the same project — about 1.3x chance, not the strong effect the raw rate suggested. Treat that ratio as a ceiling on any causal claim, since it is correlational. Prevented by: `baseline.mjs` is not optional in this skill's documented workflow — see [`SKILL.md`](../SKILL.md) — every raw-rate question routes through the placebo comparison first.

**Assuming the obvious savings are safe.** Two large ones inverted on measurement in the original analysis. Repeat emissions looked redundant but carried a *higher* write rate than first emissions (11.9% vs 5.9%). Explanatory prose looked like overhead but entries lacking it showed a 0% write rate. Prevented by: [`simulate.mjs`](../scripts/simulate.mjs) never applies a proposed policy to already-collected data as a fait accompli — it always reports characters saved *and* outcomes retained side by side, so a policy that looks cheap can be seen costing real write-outcomes before anyone builds it.

**Reading a tool failure as a data finding.** A CLI absent on a remote host, or a relative path under a non-interactive `ssh` that starts in a different directory, both yield empty results that read as "the corpus is empty". Prevented by: [`collect.mjs`](../scripts/collect.mjs)'s `--host` mode resolves the remote transcript root to an absolute path before globbing (`ssh <host> 'echo $HOME/.claude/projects'`, never `~` and shell expansion), and checks the exit code of both that resolution and the remote `tar` separately from parsing whatever came back on stdout — a failure exits non-zero with a distinct message; a transcript store that truly has zero matching files is reported as such, not conflated with a broken connection.

## Why `baseline.mjs` doesn't fit a multivariate model

The prototype that produced the original analysis's per-feature ranking used hand-rolled logistic regression (gradient descent, no standard errors). It could report a coefficient's sign and rough magnitude but never whether a difference was distinguishable from noise. `baseline.mjs` deliberately does not port this: it reports the placebo enrichment ratio (the number this skill's must-haves actually require) plus simple per-predicate crosstabs — a predicate's rate against its own placebo, not a multivariate log-odds. A wrong "which feature matters" ranking is worse than no ranking; the ratio and crosstabs are honest about exactly what they compare.

## A correction to the original transcript-shape notes

Subagent records were assumed to carry a field named `agentName`. The real field, confirmed against this repo's own local transcripts, is `agentId` (e.g. `"adeveloper-2-97d590fa983fb502"`) — `collect.mjs`'s emissions intermediate uses the real field name.
